name: Spearmint
description: Mint is an energetic and cooling herb revered for its invigorating menthol aroma. It thrives easily in garden beds and containers, offering fresh leaves for summer drinks and savory dishes.
uses: Garnish for classic Mojitos, Juleps, and lemonade
Brewed into soothing digestive herbal teas
Key herb in Middle Eastern tabbouleh and tzatziki sauces
Aromatherapy for mental focus and cooling sensation

video.title: How to Grow Mint in Containers (And Get a Huge Harvest)

uses: Mint tea is a classic remedy for indigestion, gas and queasiness
Inhaled steam or aroma traditionally used to ease a stuffy nose
Chewed leaves freshen breath and soothe the mouth
benefits: Menthol gives a cooling, calming effect on the stomach and throat
May help relax digestive muscles and ease discomfort after meals
medicinal.caution: Mint can worsen acid reflux in some people. Concentrated mint oils should not be used on or near the face of babies and young children.

taste: Cool, fresh and sweet, with a menthol tingle.
sideEffects: Can make heartburn and acid reflux worse in some people
Concentrated mint oil should not be put on or near the face of babies and young children
Large amounts of mint tea may upset the stomach

safety.allergy: Mint allergy is uncommon but possible, and people allergic to other mint-family plants can react to it. Stop using it if you get a rash, itching or swelling.
safety.pregnancy: Mint in food and tea amounts is generally considered fine. Avoid strong mint oils and ask a doctor about medicinal doses.
safety.pets: Mint can cause an upset stomach in cats and dogs, and mint oil can be harmful, so keep the plant and oils out of reach.
safety.medications: Mint can relax the muscle between the stomach and food pipe, which may worsen reflux. Ask your doctor if you take reflux or stomach medicines.

temperature: A tough, hardy plant that grows well at about 15-25 °C. It dies back in winter and returns in spring.
harvest: Cut stems in the morning once the dew has dried and before the plant flowers. Cut just above a pair of leaves and take up to half of a stem. Regular cutting keeps it bushy and productive all season.
storage: Stand the stems in a glass of water in the fridge with a loose bag on top for about a week. Mint freezes well in ice cubes, and bunches can be hung upside down in a dry place to dry.
dailyLife: Brew fresh leaves in hot water as a tea after dinner
Add to water, lemonade or yogurt for a cool taste
Chew a leaf to freshen breath
Toss into salads, tabbouleh and peas
tips: Grow it in a pot, because mint spreads fast and can take over a bed
Keep the soil moist, it dislikes drying out
Cut it back hard after flowering for a fresh flush of leaves

origin.details: Spearmint is native to southern Europe and southwest Asia and has been used since ancient times. Today it grows wild in damp places on almost every continent.
